title: Mai Mercado / Christiania 2016 — Heads and Tails Reconstruction
purpose: Put the main accounts side by side and determine what the surviving material actually supports, where narratives diverge, and which hypotheses remain unresolved.
method: Separate event facts, contemporaneous reporting, prosecution framing, Mercado statements, Son statements, later media compression, firsthand counterclaims and Potatoverse interpretation. Do not treat a later moral/theological reading as proof of an earlier factual proposition.

side_by_side.public_record: Mercado publicly celebrated police destruction of Christiania hash stalls using forceful language ('gennemsmadrer' / 'I love it').
side_by_side.son_position: He felt the post mocked or punched downward at cannabis users and wanted dialogue about medical cannabis.
side_by_side.assessment: The later 'random unprovoked threat' shorthand omits a real political trigger. This contextualizes the dispute but does not legally justify threats.

side_by_side.topic: Scale and topology of Facebook discussion
side_by_side.public_record: Many users reacted harshly; multiple later defendants arose from the same controversy.
side_by_side.son_position: Later account says one central disputed reply was directed within a multi-user argument and some later quoted statements were not his.
side_by_side.assessment: A branching thread is the correct evidentiary model. Flat quotation lists are intrinsically weaker because they lose speaker/addressee/parent structure.

side_by_side.public_record: SønderborgNYT reports he denied guilt, appealed remand, said he sought dialogue and said it was not his intention to seek Mercado out and carry out death threats.
side_by_side.son_position: Later formulation: mirror/reciprocity rather than threat; harsh rhetoric was answered with harsh rhetoric.
side_by_side.assessment: The later defense is partly corroborated contemporaneously: denial of violent intent was present at the June 2016 hearing, not invented only years later.

side_by_side.public_record: He reportedly acknowledged writing around fifteen posts on Mercado's open Facebook profile.
side_by_side.son_position: Later account emphasizes one central incriminating exchange and disputes authorship of several statements later attributed to him.
side_by_side.assessment: These are not necessarily incompatible. Fifteen total contributions may include arguments/replies that were not threats. Primary thread and charge exhibits are needed to map which statements were charged.

side_by_side.public_record: Earliest local report prints 'vil du gerne dø?' inside ellipsis-separated fragments, without parent comment or addressee.
side_by_side.son_position: Later account says this meant 'do you have a death wish / are you crazy?' as a rebuke to another commenter.
side_by_side.assessment: The language is pragmatically ambiguous. The surviving article cannot resolve speaker target or speech act because thread topology is missing.

side_by_side.public_record: Later Ritzau/JydskeVestkysten version prints a third-party formulation equivalent to understanding if 'someone' might stab Mercado and her baby.
side_by_side.son_position: Disputes authorship/context of several statements and rejects the shorthand that he personally promised to stab anyone.
side_by_side.assessment: Even if accurately attributed, third-party agency is linguistically different from 'I will stab you'. Later summaries risk speech-act hardening. Authorship remains a primary-record question.

side_by_side.public_record: After police contact, a statement says that if the matter has consequences for him it will have consequences for Mercado, 'not a threat, but a guarantee'. Court later treated conduct as witness intimidation.
side_by_side.son_position: Cause-and-effect / karma: actions create reciprocal consequences; no promise of personal violence.
side_by_side.assessment: This is a genuine interpretive conflict. The court finding is historical fact; the claimed intended meaning is separately supported by the broader contemporaneous denial of violent intent, but not thereby legally controlling.

side_by_side.public_record_a: Ritzau says another Facebook user reported the matter and Mercado said she herself did not make the police report.
side_by_side.public_record_b: SønderborgNYT reports that Folketingets security department filed the report after Mercado contacted it.
side_by_side.assessment: This is one of the strongest source conflicts. The accounts can coexist if there were multiple referrals or if Mercado initiated contact while security formally filed the complaint. It shows Mercado may have been upstream even if she did not personally submit police paperwork.

side_by_side.public_record: She was a sitting MP and had access to Folketing security; local police handled the criminal case.
side_by_side.assessment: Institutional access is real. It is not evidence by itself of control over police, PET involvement, or misuse of a secret 'political police'. The correct research question is whether her access changed the referral pathway or treatment of the case.

side_by_side.public_record: At the June 21 remand hearing, the prosecutor reportedly said Mercado and family became very worried/unsafe and hurried to Sweden to borrow a summer house.
side_by_side.project_counterclaim: The user/Son account says the Sweden trip was actually a later ordinary vacation, by which time the Son had already been detained for weeks.
side_by_side.assessment: The public source proves the flight-for-fear story was presented in court; it does not prove actual travel timing or purpose. The counterclaim is highly testable but still requires dated primary travel/media material. If the timing is as alleged, it would materially undermine the dramatic immediate-flight narrative, though not prove she felt no fear.

side_by_side.project_claim: Mercado deleted comments and later the thread after media/police involvement.
side_by_side.public_record: Current surviving articles do not provide the original Facebook tree; no recovered primary artifact yet proves exact deletion timing and scope.
side_by_side.assessment: Potentially crucial because deletion could remove speaker/addressee context. At present it is a firsthand allegation plus an observable absence, not proof of evidentiary destruction.

side_by_side.public_record: Early reports preserve some triggering context and uncertainty; later stories increasingly summarize the case as established threats and foreground Mercado's victim experience.
side_by_side.assessment: A measurable narrative inversion occurs: the politician's provocative initiating rhetoric recedes while victimhood becomes the dominant frame. This is media-framing evidence, not proof of coordinated deception.

side_by_side.public_record: An 18-year-old woman received 60 days suspended imprisonment for similar danger-warning language; a separate 17-year-old later testified that Mercado blocked and reported him.
side_by_side.assessment: The wider controversy contained distinct speakers and reporting pathways. This strengthens the need for defendant-specific attribution and weakens any generic narrative that all threats/comments belonged to one person.

side_by_side.public_record: The Son received five months unconditional imprisonment after conviction on three of four counts; the 18-year-old woman received a suspended sentence/community work.
side_by_side.assessment: The disparity is real but cannot be attributed solely to apology or refusal to plead. Age, count structure, witness-intimidation finding and personal circumstances are potential confounders.

side_by_side.public_record: Mercado was already an MP before the controversy and became minister on 28 November 2016. Ministerial office carried salary and pension rights.
side_by_side.assessment: The controversy became part of her public political biography and may have increased visibility/sympathy. That establishes benefit/salience, not motive or causal influence on appointment.

side_by_side.public_record: Mercado was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2025; a later Cancer Society account says her mother, grandmother and great-grandmother also had breast cancer and she had long considered herself at elevated risk.
side_by_side.potatoverse_interpretation: Later illness is read retrospectively as ominous/karmic correspondence with the Son's consequence language.
side_by_side.assessment: This can be recorded as a symbolic/prophetic interpretation, but it is not evidence that the universe punished Mercado or that the 2016 statements medically caused/predicted her cancer. Familial risk is an important competing factual context.

what_now_looks_strongest: The political conflict was provoked by an elected official's deliberately inflammatory public rhetoric, not an unprompted private attack.
The Son's not-guilty/no-violent-intent posture is contemporaneously documented.
The Facebook environment was multi-speaker and therefore vulnerable to attribution collapse when flattened.
The initial police-referral story has at least two materially different contemporaneous versions.
Mercado appears upstream of at least one institutional referral through Folketing security.
Later media coverage hardens legal/journalistic interpretation into simpler declarative descriptions.
The surviving public record is insufficient to authenticate every sentence, addressee and speaker without primary Facebook/court evidence.
what_does_not_follow_yet: That Mercado knowingly constructed a false flag.
That she knowingly framed the Son specifically.
That she knowingly attributed another person's words to him.
That she controlled police or used PET/political police improperly.
That Sweden was definitely a fabricated fear story.
That political promotion or pension was the motive for her conduct.
That later cancer was punishment or proof of prophecy.
best_current_model: The most defensible integrated model is a politically provoked, chaotic multi-user online conflict that entered an institutional referral system partly through Mercado and/or parliamentary security, was converted by police/prosecution into defendant-specific charges, and was then simplified by a media source chain that progressively lost thread topology and interpretive uncertainty. The Son's contemporaneous denial of violent intent and later mirror/karma account remain relevant counter-evidence to the dominant threat narrative, but the court's conviction remains part of the historical record. A deliberate false-flag theory remains possible only as a hypothesis until primary attribution/referral records show knowing manipulation.
decisive_missing_evidence: original Facebook thread/export/screenshots with reply hierarchy and edit/deletion timestamps
initial police complaint metadata identifying referrer, timestamp and attached comment
full indictment and August 2016 judgment with exhibits
original JydskeVestkysten courtroom copy and reporter notes if preserved
TV2 broadcast/transcript about reporting, fear and Sweden
dated Sweden travel/posts sufficient to reconstruct trip timeline
any lawyer notes or correspondence concerning plea advice and defense theory
